prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a passenger and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1152; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: On arrival at the intersection in Pasadena, Texas, I found two vehicles at rest after a collision during a left turn. Driver 1 stated that their vehicle was turning left when it was struck by the vehicle operated by Driver 2. Driver 2 gave the same account, and two witnesses on the scene described the sequence in the same way. Driver 2, both witnesses, and the photographs taken at the scene confirm that Passenger was seated in Driver 1's vehicle at the time of impact. Passenger reported neck strain. Damage to the rear quarter panel of Driver 1's vehicle is consistent with the impact described, and I found no earlier damage to either vehicle. Driver 1 advised that they live with the policyholder and are a listed household member. The impact appeared minor, and neither vehicle required towing. The reported injury appears severe relative to the apparent force of the collision, and this has been noted for follow-up. No citations were issued at the scene.
